notes:
Account overview:
- Large EU-headquartered fintech (licenced payments + custody) exploring Redwood Private (VPC) for regulated inference workloads.
- Primary requirement: strict data residency enforcement per region (EU-only for EU customers, separate UK boundary, Canadian residency for CA customers). APAC out of scope for initial rollout.
- Heavy focus on auditability, KMS/BYOK, and immutable audit logs retained per regulator (requested 7 years).

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-11-20: Intro / discovery call (AE Maya + SE Devon) — high-level requirements captured.
- 2025-12-08: Sent initial security questionnaire (72% complete).
- 2026-01-15: Deep-dive with infra (network, peering constraints) — customer provided VPC architecture diagram.
- 2026-02-14: Security review meeting (Fireflies ff_2026-02-14_7129). Legal flagged UK DPA text and key custody proof.
- 2026-03-02: KMS capabilities call with Redwood infra team (Fireflies ff_2026-03-02_8112).
- 2026-03-05: Updated questionnaire submitted; waiting on Redwood HSM/BYOK tech note.

Use-case details & acceptance criteria:
- Workloads: support chat for regulated users, document search over customer contracts, transaction-analysis models for fraud detection.
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for chat inference (short prompts), throughput: 500-800 qps for embeddings/recall tasks during peak batch windows.
- Cost sensitivity: Moderate — willing to pay premium for residency and SLA but expects Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce unit cost.
- Model preferences: open models (quantized), aim to pin smaller high-throughput variants for embeddings and larger verifier models for high-safety paths.
- Routing/fallback: must allow per-tenant routing policies — EU tenant traffic must not cross UK/US unless explicitly authorized. Fallback to dedicated EU pools only; no cross-border fallback by default.

Security & compliance specifics:
- Mandatory: SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning, SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence, penetration test summary, and quarterly compliance attestation.
- KMS: BYOK support required. Primary ask: integration with customer-managed AWS KMS and GCP KMS, with option for HSM-backed keys. Customer expects key rotation policies visible and an audit trail proving no plaintext key export.
- Audit logging: forward application + inference audit logs to Splunk (customer SIEM); immutable audit store for 7 years. Need proof-of-concept for log export and retention controls.
- Data residency controls: control-plane separation preferred (control plane in Redwood managed but deployed within EU tenant account or EU-controlled management plane). Data plane to be in customer VPC with strict subnet ACLs and no egress outside region.

POC plan & acceptance criteria:
- POC scope: deploy Redwood Private VPC in customer test AWS accounts (eu-west-1, eu-west-2 for UK, ca-central-1 for Canada).
- Success criteria: (1) per-tenant regional pinning works end-to-end, (2) logs are forwarded to customer Splunk with retention policy enforced, (3) BYOK integrated and HSM-backed keys used for model encryption, (4) latency targets met for lab traffic.
- Timeline: customer legal sign-off on DPA -> infra schedule for peering -> 4-week POC window (prefer May).

Notes from stakeholders (quoted):
- CTO: "We cannot move EU customer data outside EU under our regulator; need legal assurance + technical enforcement."
- Head of Security: "Show me HSM proof, KMS separation, and immutable audit chain. 7-year retention non-negotiable."
- Platform Lead: "We want per-tenant routing and the ability to pin model variants by region. Also need a migration plan for production cutover with minimal downtime."

Open items / blockers:
- Legal needs Redwood DPA amendment with UK-specific clause (SEC-1987).
- SE requires a short HSM technical note + architecture diagram for BYOK flow (INF-3241).
- Customer change freeze in April reduces available POC windows — pushing procurement target to June.
